name: Accordion
notes: Stable caller-owned IDs preserve expansion through reorder. Choose single or multiple expansion. A custom native DisclosureGroup style makes the complete header, including whitespace and the chevron, one native Button.

name: Alert
notes: A leading native stack composes CNAlertTitle, CNAlertDescription, icons, and optional actions. This inline status surface keeps its content visible without presenting a system alert.

name: Alert Dialog
notes: The system owns the alert surface and button placement. Supply native Button roles. Classes style the trigger; they do not override system alert internals.

name: Aspect Ratio
notes: A positive finite ratio sizes native child content from the available width. Put container backgrounds and corners in classes:; style the image or other child separately.

name: Attachment
notes: Uses native Link for explicit opening. The component does not read file contents. The host owns security-scoped access, file import, upload transport, and removal.

name: Avatar
notes: Native AsyncImage displays a URL or fallback on loading and error. Cropping and sizing use registered classes. Provide a meaningful accessible name.

name: Badge
notes: Compose text or custom content with primary, secondary, outline, and destructive variants. A badge displays status; wrap it in a native Button or Link when it activates an action.

name: Breadcrumb
notes: Compose native Link or NavigationLink items with CNBreadcrumbSeparator and CNBreadcrumbPage. The current page receives the selected accessibility trait. Separators remain decorative; the host owns navigation.

name: Bubble
notes: Compose text, attachments, or other native views in a styled vertical stack. CNBubbleGroup groups related content. The host supplies alignment, message identity, and any interactive actions.

name: Button
notes: A native Button preserves roles, keyboard shortcuts, disabled behavior, and custom labels. Variants and sizes use class recipes. Focus, hover, and press feedback use the editable control-motion recipe.

name: Button Group
notes: Group arbitrary native controls horizontally or vertically. Horizontal groups stack when their ideal widths exceed the available space. The same child controls and their local state remain in the layout.

name: Calendar
notes: A custom six-week SwiftUI grid uses styled day buttons and month navigation. Calendar arithmetic respects the environment calendar, locale, time zone, and daylight-saving changes. Selected, today, adjacent-month, and disabled days have separate recipes. Bounds apply to days and month navigation. Day buttons expose full date labels and selected state. External selection changes reveal that month. Override dayClasses or reuse CNCalendarDay in your own layout.

name: Card
notes: Compose CNCardHeader, CNCardTitle, CNCardDescription, CNCardContent, and CNCardFooter in a native stack. Footer actions stack when space is limited. The card itself adds no activation gesture.

name: Carousel
notes: Uses native horizontal scroll paging and stable IDs. Deleting a selected item moves selection to the first remaining page. VoiceOver provides next and previous page actions. Size the viewport with classes.

name: Chart
notes: Requires Apple Swift Charts, included in the SDK. Supply native chart marks. Classes style the surface and control tint; mark, axis, and scale APIs remain native Swift Charts APIs.

name: Checkbox
notes: The complete styled row activates the binding, including label spacing and padding. The native Toggle configuration owns checked state, while one Button handles the complete row. macOS keeps its system checkbox appearance and a 32-point minimum height. iOS uses a 44-point minimum width and height. Disabled rows cannot activate.

name: Collapsible
notes: A bound native DisclosureGroup uses a full-width Button header, including whitespace and its chevron. Supply a custom label and content. Expanded layout changes use disclosure-motion and respect Reduce Motion.

name: Combobox
notes: A searchable custom SwiftUI popover selects stable option IDs. Empty results and disabled options are handled. The selected value remains in the caller binding.

name: Command
notes: Search filters titles and details. Disabled options cannot activate. Native list selection, Return, and macOS arrow commands support keyboard use. The host owns command effects.

name: Context Menu
notes: Attach native contextual actions to any child view. The platform supplies secondary-click or long-press activation and menu dismissal. Native Button roles, shortcuts, and disabled items remain available.

name: Data Table
notes: Supply native TableColumn builders and key paths, a selection binding, and sort order. The table sorts a copy of the records. Native compact-width tables show their first column; provide a rich first cell for compact layouts.

name: Date Picker
notes: A bound native compact DatePicker handles editing and platform presentation. Choose the allowed date range and displayed date/time components. Locale, calendar, and time zone come from SwiftUI environment values.

name: Dialog
notes: Uses a native sheet rather than a web overlay. Compose headers, fields, footer actions, and CNDialogClose. The close button uses the native cancel shortcut.

name: Direction
notes: Set the native layoutDirection environment for one subtree. Leading and trailing alignment and direction-aware symbols follow that environment. The host supplies content and navigation behavior.

name: Drawer
notes: Uses a native sheet. iOS supports medium and large detents and a drag indicator. macOS retains its native sheet presentation.

name: Dropdown Menu
notes: A custom SwiftUI action surface opens in an anchored popover, including compact iOS layouts. Compose CNDropdownMenuItem, Label, Separator, Shortcut, and CheckboxItem. Arrow keys wrap through enabled items; Home and End move to the first and last item. Return activates, and Escape or outside interaction dismisses. Action items close the popover; checkbox items keep it open. A shortcut label is a visual hint; attach keyboardShortcut to install the action. Use isPresented to control presentation externally, contentClasses to style the surface, or CNDropdownMenuContent for your own presentation. Use these parts instead of native Menu items. Add .cnPopoverHost() at the screen root for the custom in-window surface and repeatable trigger clicks. Without a host, presentation uses the system popover. The popover-motion recipe controls interruptible entry and exit; repeated trigger clicks immediately reverse presentation.

name: Empty
notes: Compose a centered empty-state surface with CNEmptyTitle, CNEmptyDescription, and native actions. Use CNEmptyContent for additional content. The host decides when the empty state replaces its normal content.

name: Field
notes: Imported and copied parts share the public validation environment. Native controls retain their labels, bindings, focus, and accessibility. Use native labels or accessibilityLabel to associate field meaning.

name: Hover Card
notes: A custom SwiftUI popover opens after a short pointer delay. A delayed close allows travel from the trigger into the popover. Explicit button activation keeps the content open for keyboard and touch users. Outside interaction dismisses the popover. Supply noninteractive trigger content.

name: Input
notes: A native TextField or SecureField preserves selection, input methods, password managers, submit, and accessibility. Decoration gaps focus the same editor. Pass a FocusState binding with focus: when the host controls focus.

name: Input Group
notes: Compose CNInputGroupField with icons, addons, or native actions. Decoration gaps focus the native editor; child buttons retain their own events. Pass focus: when the host controls focus.

name: Input OTP
notes: Uses one native text field. ASCII digits are normalized and truncated on edit and paste. iOS adds one-time-code autofill and a numeric keyboard. Submit remains a native onSubmit action.

name: Item
notes: Compose leading media, CNItemContent, title, description, and CNItemActions in a native row. The row aligns content at its center. Place interactive content in native controls to define activation semantics.

name: Kbd
notes: CNKbd displays a keycap with native monospaced font design and editable classes. Place it inside the action label, then attach SwiftUI keyboardShortcut to that action control. The example opens the same searchable command dialog by click or Command-K. Choosing a result updates the label; Close or Escape dismisses the dialog.

name: Label
notes: Style localized text or custom native content with the label recipe. For an associated control label, use its native label builder or accessibilityLabel. Visual proximity alone does not establish that association.

name: Marker
notes: Conversation status rows support inline, bordered, and labeled separator variants. Icons can be decorative. Wrap the content in a native Button or Link for interactive markers.

name: Menubar
notes: An in-window strip of native Menu controls. For the macOS application menu bar, use Scene.commands. This component does not install global commands.

name: Message
notes: Compose an avatar, CNMessageContent, metadata, bubbles, and CNMessageActions in native stacks. The host owns sender identity, grouping, timestamps, and action effects. Child links and controls retain native interaction.

name: Message Scroller
notes: Preserves reading position by default. Opt into followNewMessages only while the user follows the conversation. The host owns that decision. Following uses native scroll positioning and respects Reduce Motion. Pass scrollRevision when an existing message grows during streaming.

name: Native Select
notes: An automatic native Picker binds a stable option ID. The platform chooses its presentation and keyboard behavior. Disabled options remain unavailable; supply an initial ID that belongs to the options.

name: Navigation Menu
notes: Compose native links, navigation links, and submenu controls in a horizontal ScrollView. The menu keeps its contents reachable at narrow widths. The host owns the navigation path and destinations.

name: Pagination
notes: Page numbers are one-based. The visible window stays bounded for large page counts. A page count of zero disables navigation and normalizes the binding to zero.

name: Popover
notes: A native button toggles a custom SwiftUI popover. Choose its preferred side and compose arbitrary content. Classes style the trigger. Add .cnPopoverHost() at the screen root for custom in-window presentation beyond scrolling children. Without a host, presentation uses the system popover. The popover-motion recipe controls interruptible entry and exit. Outside interaction dismisses the surface.

name: Progress
notes: A native ProgressView supports determinate values or an indeterminate nil value. Finite positive totals define the range; values are clamped. Determinate changes use feedback-motion and respect Reduce Motion.

name: Questionnaire
notes: The host owns ordered questions, answers, active index, cancellation, and submission. Required, type, single-choice, and available-option validation runs before submission. IDs must be unique. Branching, transport, and persistence belong to the host.

name: Radio Group
notes: Uses a native radio-group Picker on macOS and an inline native Picker on iOS. It supports long option lists without forcing a segmented control.

name: Resizable
notes: Only the divider captures drag gestures. It tracks the pointer immediately in a stable coordinate space and preserves the grab offset. Horizontal, vertical, and right-to-left layouts support a normalized binding, minimum fractions, and accessible adjustment. Drag updates suppress inherited animations; release and cancellation clear the grab. Disabled splits ignore dragging and accessible adjustment. Size the container with classes.

name: Scroll Area
notes: A native ScrollView supports vertical, horizontal, or combined axes and optional indicators. Child controls retain their gestures. Compose lazy stacks when the collection is large; the host owns scroll-position policies.

name: Select
notes: A native menu-style Picker binds a stable option ID. Disabled options remain unavailable. Supply an initial ID that belongs to the options; SwiftUI owns keyboard activation and menu presentation.

name: Separator
notes: Display a decorative native divider in a horizontal or vertical orientation. Classes control its color and dimensions. It remains hidden from accessibility; provide meaningful headings or labels for section semantics.

name: Sheet
notes: Uses native sheet presentation and dismissal. Presentations keep keyboard, focus, modality, accessibility, and environment behavior in SwiftUI.

name: Sidebar
notes: A custom SwiftUI sidebar composes pinned headers and footers, scrollable groups, selected menu buttons, badges, and nested menus. Desktop visibility supports icon rails, offcanvas collapse, or a fixed panel. Compact widths use a separate controlled or local drawer state; outside activation, menu selection, Escape, and a horizontal swipe dismiss it. Native buttons retain focus, disabled state, roles, and accessibility. The detail and sidebar remain mounted through reversible transitions. Set sidebar-motion to animate-none in global rules to disable motion; presets also respect Reduce Motion. The host owns navigation destinations and selection.

name: Skeleton
notes: Native redaction keeps the same controls mounted while a subtle gradient shimmers across the placeholder. Loading content stays disabled and hidden from accessibility. The skeleton-motion recipe uses cn-shimmer-[1.6], in seconds; set it to cn-shimmer-[0] to stop shimmer. The native timeline pauses offscreen, in inactive scenes, and under Reduce Motion. Use cnLoadingPhase for reproducible static previews.

name: Slider
notes: A native Slider binds a Double within the supplied range and positive finite step. onEditingChanged reports editing boundaries. Native pointer, touch, keyboard, and accessibility adjustment remain available.

name: Spinner
notes: A custom circular ring uses a rounded arc and quiet track. Its label describes activity to accessibility without adding visible text. Classes control size and color; lineWidth controls the stroke. The spinner-motion recipe uses cn-spin-[0.9], in seconds; cn-spin-[0] pauses it. Native timeline updates stop offscreen, in inactive scenes, and under Reduce Motion. Use cnLoadingPhase for reproducible static previews.

name: Switch
notes: The complete styled row activates the binding. The system switch keeps its native thumb gesture, keyboard handling, accessibility, and disabled behavior. Row taps outside the system indicator activate the binding. The system indicator handles its own gestures without duplicate activation.

name: Table
notes: Compose rich aligned columns with native Grid, GridRow, CNTableHead, and CNTableCell parts. The table fills its viewport and scrolls horizontally when columns need more room. Header cells expose accessibility headings. Rows have separators, immediate hover feedback, and a caller-controlled selected appearance. Cells accept leading, center, or trailing alignment. CNTableCaption adds supporting text outside the table. Pass onSelect: to make row whitespace selectable. Child checkboxes, buttons, and editors handle their own events without also activating the row; use CNDataTable for native record sorting.

name: Tabs
notes: Uses native TabView with caller-supplied tagged views. Each tab can contain arbitrary SwiftUI content. Use native tabItem and tag modifiers.

name: Textarea
notes: A native TextEditor preserves multiline editing, selection, input methods, and scrolling. Pass focus: when the host controls focus. The field recipe supplies focus and disabled feedback; provide a meaningful accessible label.

name: Toast
notes: The host owns one optional toast per window. Replacement cancels the old timeout; identity checks prevent an older task from dismissing a newer toast. Nil duration requires explicit dismissal. Native accessibility announcements expose new notifications without moving editing focus.

name: Toggle
notes: A native Toggle configuration uses a styled Button for the entire padded activation surface. The binding and checked accessibility state stay native. Selected and unselected recipes remain editable through classes.

name: Toggle Group
notes: Compose button-style native toggles from stable option IDs and a Set binding. Disabled options cannot activate. The action layout adapts to narrow space while preserving the controls and their state.

name: Tooltip
notes: Uses native help on macOS. On iOS, the label becomes a native button that opens a descriptive popover. Supply noninteractive label content.

name: Typography
notes: Style localized native Text with title, heading, body, lead, small, muted, or code variants. Title and heading variants expose the header accessibility trait. Code uses native monospaced font design.
